newsitem.title: FINLAND: Analysts cautious on Enso Holtzmann deal.
newsitem.headline: Analysts cautious on Enso Holtzmann deal.

text.p: Finnish paper group Enso Oy's purchase of a majority interest in German printing paper group E. Holtzmann marked further consolidation in the sector, analysts said on Monday, but views were mixed on the price.

Enso said it paid 1.8 billion markka for 50.4 percent of the debt-free German group, which analysts said would increase the strain on Enso's balance sheet at a time when there is uncertainty about paper prices and profitability this year and next.
Enso itself said the about 5,000 markka per tonne it paid was cheaper than recent deals and the investment would at some point meet its 12 percent return on investment target.
"At least in 1997, it definitely will not," said Lars Kjellberg, analyst at Enskilda in Stockholm. "I think hardly anyone will reach that this year."

Last year, Holtzmann -- which has a capacity of 700,000 tonnes per year of newsprint and uncoated magazine paper -- made a 580 million markka operating profit and net sales totalled 2.46 billion markka.
"This year, it will be significantly lower," Kjellberg said. "The price seems high in the short term at least."
Enso said it expected the group's operating profit to fall this year along with prices, but that it nonetheless expected the deal to boost earnings per share.
Analysts declined to give any recommendations on its stock but said higher EPS would not automatically change anything, and some said they had yet to reach a conclusion.
By the early afternoon, Enso's shares were off 0.50 markka at 43.00 and trade was thin at about one million markka.
AG Pankkiiriliike analyst Jussi Hyoty said buying existing capacity in the paper industry is always a welcome consolidation, and that the grades acquired would be a good fit for Enso.
"The price seems rather fair to me, it could even be better than fair," Hyoty said, seeing three factors favouring the deal.
"It is a debt-free company which in Europe is very rare, EBIT (operating profit) last year was 24 percent of net sales which is very good .... and the grade base here is OK," he said.

On the downside, the timing of such a big purchase was questionable since it is not clear whether an expected upturn in paper prices would actually emerge -- they could even turn lower next year, Hyoty said.
"On the other hand, (this deal) signals that Enso's management does not expect that to happen," he added.
Merita analyst Pertti Aaltonen agreed that Holtzmann would fit Enso and found the price acceptable.
"It seems like a good purchase because of the market position and because of this new product (uncoated magazine paper) they haven't had so far," Aaltonen said.

Enso said it expected to reach synergy benefits of 170 million markka by 1999, but Kjellberg said this looked high compared to the 350 million markka in savings Enso reached through its 1995 merger with state-owned Veitsiluoto.
"On the whole, I am neutral on this deal, but I would say it is surprising since this (newsprint and uncoated magazine papers) is not a segment where consolidation is needed," he said.
